findings.title: Guiding chart Y axis draws two labels on top of each other when the series is flat
findings.what_happened: With all three frames at guiding RMS 0.70, the Guiding performance axis renders 0.25 and 0.20 overlapping into an illegible blob at the bottom of the axis.
findings.expected: Axis labels never overlap - which is exactly what NiceAxis was written to guarantee.
findings.repro: Seed frames with identical guiding_rms_total (0.70); Analytics > Session; look at the bottom-left of the Guiding performance chart.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-06-guideaxis.png
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/chart_axis.dart:33-43 (zero-variance branch)
findings.proposed_fix: The zero-variance branch returns min = centre - 2*interval without snapping to a tick multiple (0.70 - 0.50 = 0.20 with interval 0.25), so the boundary label lands 0.05 from the 0.25 tick. Snap: min = (centre/interval).floor()*interval - 2*interval, same for max - the same snapping the varying branch already does.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Three frames all at guiding_rms_total = 0.70; the Guiding performance axis renders '0.25' and '0.20' printed on top of each other at the bottom (native-res crop /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2a-08-guideaxis-070.png). Root cause is at the cited location, chart_axis.dart:31-43: the zero-variance branch returns min = centre - interval*2 (0.70-0.50 = 0.20), which is not a multiple of the interval (0.25), so fl_chart's boundary label lands a fraction of a tick from the outermost tick - the exact failure the class doc-comment says NiceAxis exists to prevent (the non-degenerate branch snaps min/max to interval multiples; the degenerate branch does not). Not unique to guiding: a 0.60 series prints '1.10' touching '1.00', and Focus drift prints '15240' touching '15200'.

findings.title: The four Session charts are computed over three different frame populations; the guiding chart includes frames the app rejected

The guiding headline therefore reads median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 and the 1" warning line is breached, when every accepted frame guided between 0.50" and 0.95". A p90 of 3.9" for a session whose accepted-frame p90 is 0.905" is a wrong number a user would act on (they would go hunting for a guiding fault that does not exist).

Analytics > Session > Night A - M31 renders exactly the claimed headers: Image quality n=10, Guiding performance median 0.8 / p90 3.9 / range 0.5-4.2 / n=12, Focus drift n=12, Sensor temperature n=16, beside a strip reading EXPOSURES 10/12. findings.title: Exported FWHM is fabricated from HFR with the wrong factor (2.35x instead of 2x), overstating FWHM by 18%
findings.what_happened: History > Night A - M31 > Export CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv with a populated "FWHM (px)" column - 4.70, 5.17, 5.64 - even though captured_images.fwhm is NULL for every one of those rows. The values are HFR * 2.35.
findings.expected: For a Gaussian PSF the half-flux radius is 1.1774*sigma and FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.00 * HFR. Multiplying HFR by 2.3548 treats HFR as sigma and inflates every reported FWHM by 17.7% (HFR 2.00 px -> 4.70" reported vs 4.00" true). Worse, the real `fwhm` column measured by the pipeline is ignored and overwritten by the derived number, and nothing in the CSV says the value is derived.
findings.repro: Analytics > History > click Night A - M31 > click the spreadsheet icon; open the CSV. HFR column x 2.35 == FWHM column exactly.
findings.evidence: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/Night A - M31_2026-08-01T14-40-26.csv rows s1_000..s1_009; DB: select hfr,fwhm from captured_images where session_id=1 -> fwhm all NULL
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_export_service.dart:69-70 and :171; same factor in session_report_service.dart:301 (meanFwhm), capture_preview_loader.dart:180 (live capture FWHM readout), session_report.dart:36
findings.proposed_fix: Use image.fwhm when present; otherwise derive FWHM = 2.0 * HFR and label the column "FWHM (px, derived from HFR)". Fix the constant in all four call sites - the live capture readout is showing the same inflated number during a run.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with my own fresh export rather than the reporter's file: History > Night A - M31 > fileSpreadsheet wrote 'Night A - M31_2026-08-02T12-05-18.csv' and every row's FWHM/HFR ratio is exactly 2.35 (2.00->4.70, 3.80->8.93, 9.90->23.27). `select count(*), count(fwhm) from captured_images where session_id=1` returns 16|0, so the column is fabricated, not read. session_export_service.dart:70 is verbatim `final fwhm = image.hfr != null ? image.hfr! * 2.35 : null;`, repeated at :171 for the JSON export, with the same factor at session_report_service.dart:301 and capture_preview_loader.dart:180. I checked the physics independently instead of accepting it: native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs:672 documents and implements calculate_hfr_at_point as the true encircled-energy 50% half-flux RADIUS ('matches the NINA / SGP / PixInsight HFR convention'), and for a Gaussian that radius is sqrt(2 ln 2)*sigma = 1.1774*sigma while FWHM = 2.3548*sigma, so FWHM = 2.000*HFR and the 2.3548 factor treats a radius as a sigma - a 17.74% inflation, matching the claimed 17.7%. The 'measured column ignored' claim holds beyond this seed: imaging_service/persistence.dart:196 and imaging_records_repository.dart:420 do write a real fwhm and the exporter never reads it. Two nits: the cited evidence file ..._14-40-26.csv does not exist (the reporter's actual file is ..._14-39-48.csv), and the cited range 69-70 is really just line 70 (69 is the comment).

findings.title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is stored outside the profile data dir, so one instance offers to resume another instance's sequence
findings.what_happened: On startup this audit instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR = /tmp/ns-audit/r-analytics/data, with ZERO rows in sequences and sequence_checkpoints) showed 'Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed - Sequence: New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'. The checkpoint it read is /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint, written by a DIFFERENT concurrently-running instance.
findings.expected: Crash recovery must be scoped to the instance/profile that wrote it. Offering to resume a sequence whose id does not exist in this database is a data-integrity hazard: on a machine that runs both the desktop app and the headless host (a shipped configuration) the two silently clobber each other's recovery state, and Resume would restart the wrong run. Note also the self-contradictory summary line 'Completed 4 frames (0m integration)'.
findings.repro: Run two Skotiq desktop instances with different SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR values. Build a sequence in one. Restart the other: it offers to recover the first one's sequence.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-analytics-33-sci2.png; sqlite3 <profile db> 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> 0 rows, 'select * from sequences' -> 0 rows; the checkpoint file in ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop was last written at 14:50 by another pid
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:347 getApplicationSupportDirectory() is passed to sequencerSetCheckpointDir, ignoring SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR; native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/checkpoint.rs:516
findings.proposed_fix: Derive the checkpoint dir from the same root as the database (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when set), and stamp the checkpoint with the database path/instance id so a mismatched checkpoint is ignored rather than offered.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Confirmed by direct experiment. First, my own instance's log reads 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' even though SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR both point at /tmp/ns-audit/v-analytics/data - getApplicationSupportDirectory() ignores both. Then I proved the read side: I planted a resumable checkpoint (sequence id 'claude-noop-probe', name 'NOOP CONTRACT PROBE') at ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint - the file another instance would write - and restarted against a database with 0 rows in sequences and 0 in sequence_checkpoints. It came up on 'Recover Sequence? / A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. / Sequence NOOP CONTRACT PROBE / Saved 0m ago' with a live Resume button, for a sequence absent from its own database. I removed the planted file afterwards. Two corrections. (1) The justification 'on a machine that runs both the desktop app and the headless host (a shipped configuration) the two silently clobber each other' does NOT hold as written: app_shell.dart is the only caller of sequencerSetCheckpointDir in the app, the headless entry point never sets it, and app_shell's `backend is! NetworkBackend` guard already avoids pushing this path at a remote host. The collision I reproduced needs two local instances with different SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR values - the audit harness's configuration, not a shipped one. (2) I cannot corroborate the secondary 'Completed 4 frames (0m integration)' observation; in my run those figures were the ones I planted, so that line proves nothing about the writer. Severity corrected to P2: the durable defect is that crash-recovery state is not scoped to the database it references, so the app will offer to resume a sequence that does not exist in the active DB, but the single-instance shipped path recovers correctly and nothing is destroyed.
findings.location_wrong: The `where` (app_shell.dart:347-348 getApplicationSupportDirectory -> sequencerSetCheckpointDir; checkpoint.rs:516) is exact. The `unit` is not: it is filed under screen:analytics/session_tab.dart and has nothing to do with the Session tab or Analytics - this is app startup.

After the startup recovery flow ran it became status='aborted' with end_time = 2026-08-01 18:52Z - the moment of recovery, 46 hours after the last frame. Its History card and every derived statistic (wall clock, effective imaging, campaign efficiency) now use a 46-hour session.
findings.expected: Closing an abandoned session should set end_time to the last captured frame's timestamp, not to the clock at recovery time. Otherwise one crash permanently corrupts the night's duration and drags the target's campaign efficiency toward zero.

findings.where: session recovery path in packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/session_service.dart (stale 'active' session handling around :431)
findings.proposed_fix: end_time = max(last captured_images.captured_at for the session, start_time) when force-closing a recovered session.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a clock check. Session 5 (Night E - M13) was left status='active', end_time NULL, last frame captured_at 1785575100 = 2026-08-01 09:05:00 UTC. I restarted the app; the startup 'Incomplete Sessions Found' dialog offered it (showing '60h 13m') and I pressed Discard. sqlite immediately after: status='aborted', end_time = 1785791645 = 2026-08-03 21:14:05 UTC, with `date -u` reading 2026-08-03 21:14:12 UTC at that moment. The abandoned session was closed 60 hours after its last frame, and every endTime-derived figure now uses that 60-hour wall clock.
findings.location_wrong: session_service.dart:431 is only the SCAN for stale rows ('// Find sessions with active status') and writes nothing. findings.title: BLS card gives no significance verdict, and its only significance number (SDE) scores pure noise higher than a textbook-strong periodic signal
findings.what_happened: Three controlled runs on the same 80-point, 118.5-minute light curve in Analytics > Science > Period Analysis. (A) pure noise: Lomb-Scargle 21.2 min, power 0.07, FAP 0.3366, no badge; BLS 21.8 min, Depth -53.6 mmag, SDE 2.7. (B) injected sinusoid P=20.0 min, amplitude 0.10 mag: LS 19.8 min, power 0.97, FAP < 1e-10, badge 'Strong'; BLS 20.1 min, Depth -115.9 mmag, SDE 2.5. (C) injected box transit P=20.0 min, depth +0.150 mag, duration 2.4 min: LS 19.8 min, FAP 9.6e-5, 'Strong'; BLS 20.0 min, Depth 151.2 mmag, SDE 4.82. So the SDE of PURE NOISE (2.7) is HIGHER than the SDE of a signal the app itself calls Strong with FAP < 1e-10 (2.5), and a genuine transit only reaches 4.8. The BLS half of the card shows no badge, no threshold and no verdict of any kind - just the bare number.
findings.expected: Either show the BLS SDE with the threshold the code itself documents ('SDE > ~6 is typically considered a significant detection', period_analysis_service.dart:81) and a verdict badge like the LS side has, or do not present SDE as a headline. As shipped a user comparing 2.7 and 2.5 would conclude the noise run is the better candidate.
findings.repro: Seed 80 photometry_measurements at 90s cadence for the selected session with (A) gaussian noise, then (B) 0.10*sin(2*pi*t/1200s), then (C) a +0.15 mag box of width 0.12 phase at P=1200s. Restart between each. Analytics > Science > Period Analysis > Run Period Search and read the BLS block.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-01.png (noise: Depth -53.6 mmag, SDE 2.7); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-19-period-signal.png (sinusoid: LS 'Strong' FAP < 1e-10, BLS SDE 2.5); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-24-blsbox.png (box transit: Period 20.0 min, Duration 2.5 min, Depth 151.2 mmag, SDE 4.82, Mid-phase 0.487)
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/period_analysis_service.dart:604-621 (SDE = (peakSR - meanSR)/stdSR over the SR spectrum) and packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/period_analysis_panel/result_widgets.dart (BLS block renders SDE with no threshold or badge)
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the SR spectrum's mean/std with the peak's own neighbourhood masked out (the standard BLS-SDE practice) so a coherent signal does not inflate its own baseline, then render a badge on the same rules the LS side uses: SDE >= 7 strong, 5-7 marginal, < 5 not significant. Show the threshold in the card.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The substantive half fully reproduces, checked by INDEPENDENT recomputation rather than by trusting the app: I ported computeBls (period_analysis_service.dart:445-637) to Python and ran it on three 80-point, 118.5-minute light curves at 90 s cadence with the app's own parameters (minP 0.01 d, maxP = 0.0823 d baseline, nbins 200, err 0.008). The port reproduces the app's on-screen noise result exactly (app: 31.4 min / 1.9 min / -54.1 mmag / SDE 3.11; port: 31.408 / 1.885 / -54.05 / 3.112), validating it. Results: (A) pure gaussian noise sigma=0.03 -> SDE 3.11; (B) injected sinusoid P=20 min amplitude 0.10 mag -> best period 21.0 min, SDE 2.56; (C) injected box transit P=20 min depth +0.150 mag -> 19.9 min, depth +153.9 mmag, SDE 4.80. Pure noise (3.11) still outscores a strong injected periodic signal (2.56), and a genuine transit reaches only 4.80 - below the code's own documented threshold (':81 SDE > ~6 is typically considered a significant detection'). Same ordering as the claim's 2.7 / 2.5 / 4.82. PARTIAL FIX SINCE FILING: the panel now computes a BLS verdict (period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599: sde > 7 -> Strong, sde > 6 -> Noteworthy), so 'no verdict of any kind' is no longer literally true - but because a real transit only scores 4.8 on this implementation the badge never fires in practice, and the card still shows a bare 'SDE: 3.11' with no threshold beside it.
findings.location_wrong: period_analysis_service.dart:604-621 (the SDE formula) is right. The UI half is not in period_analysis_panel/result_widgets.dart - that file only defines the _ResultColumn/_Verdict rendering; whether a BLS verdict is shown is decided at period_analysis_panel.dart:592-599 (blsVerdict) and the SDE string is built at :620.

findings.title: "Box Least Squares (Transit Search)" reports negative transit depths, i.e. it presents a brightening as a transit
findings.what_happened: For pure noise the BLS block read 'Depth: -53.6 mmag' and for an injected sinusoid 'Depth: -115.9 mmag'. A negative depth means the best-fitting box is BRIGHTER than the out-of-box baseline - an anti-transit. The card labels it 'Depth' under the heading 'Box Least Squares (Transit Search)' with no sign explanation and no warning. Only when a genuine box transit was injected did the sign flip positive (151.2 mmag for an injected 150 mmag).
findings.expected: A transit search should either restrict the box search to fainter-than-baseline solutions, or clearly flag a negative-depth solution as an anti-transit / brightening event rather than presenting it as the session's transit result.

findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-01.png ('Depth: -53.6 mmag | SDE: 2.7'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-19-period-signal.png ('Depth: -115.9 mmag | SDE: 2.5'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-24-blsbox.png (positive 151.2 mmag for a real transit)
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/science/period_analysis_service.dart:536-545 maximises SR = s^2/(r(1-r)), which is sign-blind, and :597 sets globalBestDepth = inTransitMean - outTransitMean without constraining the sign
findings.proposed_fix: Reject box solutions where s < 0 (in-box brighter) when the mode is transit search, or render negative depths as 'Brightening candidate (anti-transit): 115.9 mmag' so the user is not told a transit was found.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Live: on 80 pure-noise points the BLS block reads 'Period 31.4 min | Duration 1.9 min | Depth -54.1 mmag | SDE 3.11 | Mid-phase 0.325' under the heading 'Box Least Squares (Transit Search)', with no sign explanation and no warning. findings.title: Photometry CSV export writes local wall-clock timestamps with no timezone, silently shifting every measurement by the observer's UTC offset

findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and checked against the DB rather than another app readout. findings.title: Campaign Rollup contradicts itself three ways on one card: "Total integration 0.0h" beside "0.17h integration", and "No frames captured for this target yet" beside a session with 2 frames

The Campaign Rollup dialog shows header tiles 'Sessions 1', 'Total integration 0.0h', 'Mean HFR 2.20', 'Effective imaging 0.0%'; then 'Per-filter progress: No frames captured for this target yet.'; then a Sessions list containing 'Night E - M13, Jul 31 2026 23:00 | - | 0.17h integration, HFR 2.20, RMS 0.60'. findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. The M13 campaign card opens 'Campaign Rollup / M13' showing Sessions 1, Total integration 0.0h, Mean HFR 2.20, Mean seeing -, Effective imaging 0.0%, then 'Per-filter progress: No frames captured for this target yet.', then 'Night E - M13 / Jul 31, 2026 23:00 | - | 0.17h integration / HFR 2.20 / RMS 0.60'. Recomputed rather than compared: session 5 (target_id=4 = M13) has exactly 2 captured_images rows, both frame_type='light', exposure_duration 300.0, is_accepted=0, with imaging_sessions.total_integration_secs = 600.0; 600/3600 = 0.1667 -> the 0.17h row, and the accepted-light sum is 0.0 -> the 0.0h header. campaign_rollup_service.dart computes lightFrames as `frameType == 'light' && i.isAccepted`, feeding both totalCapturedIntegrationSecs (campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:172) and _buildFilters (empty -> the :226 'No frames captured' string), while the session row at campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:600 prints session.sessionIntegrationSecs. Both cited files are right. Correction for the fixer: the finding says 'the header tiles ... count only accepted frames', but only Total integration does - Mean HFR 2.20 and Effective imaging 0.0% come from the imaging_sessions rows with no acceptance filter, so the card mixes three populations, not two. Severity corrected DOWN to P2: each number is individually defensible (0.0h is the accepted integration; 0.17h is the captured integration), nothing downstream acts on it, and the defect is that one card labels different populations with the same words - sharpest in the flatly false 'No frames captured for this target yet.'
